 In Lectures on the Origin and Growth ofReligion as Illustrated by Celtic Heathendom,
2nd ed. ( 1882), John Rhys discusses the boar which killed Diarmuid in Irish
mythology as well as "other mythic swine." In The Golden Bough: A Study in
Comparative Religion (18go), James G. Frazer notes that in various cultures
the pig is an embodiment of the "corn-spirit": "the corn-spirit is conceived
as embodied in an animal; this divine animal is slain, and its flesh and blood
are partaken of by the harvesters. Thus ... the pig is eaten sacramentally
by ploughmen in the spring."
